name: TPS563200DDCR
title: TPS562200 and TPS563200: 4.5 V to 17 V input, 2 A and 3 A synchronous buck converters in 6-pin SOT-23
summary: Two synchronous step-down converters with both power switches inside a 6-pin SOT-23 (DDC): the TPS562200 delivers 2 A and the TPS563200 3 A. They run from 4.5 V to 17 V and set outputs from 0.76 V to 7 V with a two-resistor divider on a 0.765 V feedback threshold. D-CAP2 adaptive on-time control at about 650 kHz needs no compensation network and works with all-ceramic output capacitors; at light load Advanced Eco-mode skips pulses to hold efficiency. Soft start is fixed at 1 ms, and current limit, hiccup undervoltage, overvoltage, UVLO and thermal shutdown are built in.

notes: TPS562200 is the 2 A device (122 mΩ high-side, 72 mΩ low-side FET); TPS563200 is the 3 A device (68 mΩ and 39 mΩ). Both share the pinout, control scheme and 650 kHz switching frequency.
DDCR is a 3000-piece large reel and DDCT a 250-piece small reel.
Misprint: the device information lists the package as DRL (SOT-236, 6); it should read DDC (SOT-23-THIN, 6).

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground for the control circuit and source of the low-side power NFET. Return the VFB divider to this pin at one point.

pins.name: SW
pins.function: Switch node: the junction of the high-side and low-side NFETs, and the output inductor's connection.

pins.name: VIN
pins.function: Supply input; drain of the high-side power NFET.

pins.name: VFB
pins.function: Feedback input from a resistor divider across the output.

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Enable, active high. It has to be pulled up for the converter to run.

pins.name: VBST
pins.function: Supply to the gate driver of the high-side NFET; a 0.1 µF capacitor goes from VBST to SW.

notes: Top view: pins 1, 2, 3 (GND, SW, VIN) run down one side and pins 4, 5, 6 (VFB, EN, VBST) back up the other, pin 6 opposite pin 1.

circuits.description: The minimum circuit around either device: an input capacitor on VIN, a bootstrap capacitor from VBST to SW, an LC output filter from SW, a divider from the output to VFB, and EN taken to a control signal.
notes: The same circuit serves the TPS562200 and the TPS563200.

operation.text: Synchronous buck converters with both power MOSFETs inside: the TPS562200 handles 2 A and the TPS563200 3 A. The D-CAP2 control loop needs no external compensation and is stable with low-ESR output capacitors, including polymer types and multilayer ceramics; its quick transient response lets a smaller output capacitance meet a given performance target.

Every cycle begins by turning on the high-side MOSFET, which stays on until a one-shot timer runs out. The one-shot length scales with VO and inversely with VIN, which holds the switching frequency roughly constant (pseudo-fixed) as the input changes. When the feedback voltage drops under the reference, the timer restarts and the high-side switch turns on again. An internal ramp added to the reference stands in for output ripple, so the loop does not need ripple from capacitor ESR and stays stable with almost no ripple at the output.

Light-load efficiency is kept high by Advanced Eco-mode. When the inductor current's valley falls to zero (the edge of discontinuous conduction), the low-side MOSFET is turned off on zero-current detection, and lighter loads run discontinuously. The on-time is held near its continuous-mode value, so the output capacitor needs longer to fall back to the reference and the switching frequency falls in proportion to load. After each pulse the device sleeps until VFB drops below the Eco-mode threshold.

With VIN above the UVLO threshold and EN above its threshold, the converter switches normally. When the switch current never reaches 0 A it runs in continuous conduction mode at a quasi-fixed 650 kHz.

Soft start is internal and fixed at 1 ms: when EN goes high the reference fed to the PWM comparator ramps up. If the output already holds a voltage at start-up, the device starts switching only once the ramping reference passes the voltage on VFB, so the output climbs smoothly into regulation.

EN is active high and has to be pulled up for the device to run; it shows a resistance to GND of 450 kΩ typ. Driving EN low puts the converter in standby from either continuous or Eco-mode operation, drawing 3 µA typ (10 µA max) from VIN.

Current limiting is cycle by cycle on the valley of the switch current, which is sensed during the off time from the low-side FET's drain-source voltage, temperature compensated. A new on-pulse is withheld, with the low-side FET kept on, for as long as the sensed current exceeds the OCL level, whatever the feedback loop demands; after that the on-time is fixed and monitoring continues. Overcurrent on consecutive cycles lowers the OCL threshold and so the available current; a single cycle below the lower threshold restores the higher one. The load current exceeds the OCL threshold by half the peak-to-peak inductor ripple. While current is limited the output voltage can fall.

If VFB falls below the UVP threshold (65 % of the feedback threshold), the device shuts down after a delay of about 14 µs and restarts after a hiccup time of about 12 ms. Once the overload is gone the output returns to regulation.
When VFB rises above 125 % of its target, both the high-side and low-side drivers are turned off. The protection does not latch.

Undervoltage lockout watches the internal regulator voltage and turns the device off while it is under the UVLO threshold; it does not latch. The VIN wake-up threshold is 3.75 V typ with 0.32 V typ hysteresis.
Above the shutdown temperature (155 °C typ, 35 °C hysteresis) the device turns off. The protection does not latch.
The input range is 4.5 V to 17 V and has to stay above the output voltage. The highest recommended duty cycle is 65 %, which puts the lowest recommended input at VO / 0.65.

Choose L from the recommended component tables, then work out ripple, peak and RMS current with fSW = 650 kHz. The saturation rating must exceed the peak current and the RMS (heating) rating the RMS current. In the TPS562200 example (1.05 V, 2 A) the peak is 2.34 A and the RMS 2.01 A, met by a TDK CLF7045T-2R2N rated 5.5 A peak and 4.3 A RMS. In the TPS563200 example (1.05 V, 3 A) the peak is 3.505 A and the RMS 3.014 A, met by a TDK CLF7045T-1R5N rated 7.3 A peak and 4.9 A RMS.

Output ripple depends on the capacitance and its ESR. Ceramic capacitors, or others with low ESR, are intended, from 20 µF to 68 µF in total. The examples use TDK C3216X5R0J226M 22 µF parts, about 2 mΩ ESR each and each rated for 4 A: two on the TPS562200, with 0.286 A RMS calculated, and three on the TPS563200, with 0.292 A calculated.

Below the LC double pole the loop gain is fixed by the feedback divider and the device's internal gain, and the phase is 180 degrees. Above the double pole the gain falls at -40 dB per decade and the phase falls fast. A high-frequency zero in the D-CAP2 loop returns the slope to -20 dB per decade, and the phase reaches 90 degrees one decade above that zero.

An input decoupling capacitor is required, a ceramic of more than 10 µF; a bulk capacitor may be needed depending on the application. A further optional 0.1 µF from pin 3 to ground adds high-frequency filtering. Voltage ratings must exceed the highest input voltage.
A 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor between VBST and SW is required for correct operation.

Make the VIN and GND traces as wide as possible, for low impedance and for heat spreading. Place the input and output capacitors right next to the IC, with enough vias for each. Keep the SW trace short and wide to limit radiated emission, and keep switching current from flowing under the device. Run a separate trace from VOUT to the upper feedback resistor, and take the feedback return to GND as a Kelvin connection at the pin. Route the feedback loop away from the switching trace, ideally with a ground shield, and keep the VFB node small to avoid picking up noise. The ground path from the output capacitor back to pin 1 should be as wide as it can be. The example layout places the high-frequency input bypass right at VIN and GND, the boost capacitor beside VBST, the feedback resistors beside VFB, and joins SW to an inner or bottom-layer copper pour through vias, with extra vias to the GND plane at the output capacitor.
